blocks.text: Medium-vessel vasculitis involves inflammation of medium-sized arteries, leading to vascular damage, stenosis, and aneurysms. The two main types of medium vessel vasculitides are Polyarteritis Nodosa (PAN) and Kawasaki Disease.

Hypermobility and Associated Connective Tissue Disorders

Hypermobility refers to excessive joint movement beyond the normal range, often associated with connective tissue disorders such as Joint Hypermobility Syndrome (JHS) and Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS). Symptoms include joint pain, instability, dislocations, and soft tissue injury. Co-existing neurodivergent features are common. Management focuses on symptom control, functional improvement, and the prevention of complications. The Beighton Score is commonly used for assessing joint hypermobility

blocks.text: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) refers to a group of inflammatory joint disorders that begin before the age of 16 and last for more than 6 weeks. It is characterized by chronic inflammation of the synovium, which can lead to joint destruction, deformity, and functional impairment. The cause of JIA is not fully understood, but it involves genetic and environmental factors that trigger an autoimmune response in genetically predisposed children.

blocks.text: APS is an autoimmune disorder characterized by persistent antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL), leading to increased risk of thrombosis (arterial, venous, or microvascular) and pregnancy-related complications such as recurrent miscarriage, preterm birth, and preeclampsia. It may occur as a primary condition or secondary to other autoimmune diseases, particularly SLE and, less commonly, RA.

blocks.text: Fibromyalgia is a chronic pain syndrome characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain lasting ≥3 months, associated with fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive dysfunction.

runs.text: with fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive dysfunction.

blocks.text: It is a disorder of central pain processing (central sensitization) rather than peripheral inflammation.

The 2016 Revised ACR Fibromyalgia Diagnostic Criteria assist in diagnosing fibromyalgia. Tender point examination is no longer required; diagnosis is based on the Widespread Pain Index (WPI) and Symptom Severity Score (SSS) with symptoms present for at least 3 months.

runs.text: The 2016 Revised ACR Fibromyalgia Diagnostic Criteria assist in diagnosing fibromyalgia. Tender point examination is no longer required; diagnosis is based on the Widespread Pain Index (WPI) and Symptom Severity Score (SSS) with symptoms present for at least 3 months.

blocks.text: Laboratory testing should be limited to excluding alternative diagnoses when clinically indicated.
Vitamin D testing may be considered in selected patients.
Autoimmune serology should not be ordered routinely unless clinical suspicion exists.
Fibromyalgia management should be multimodal and individualized, prioritizing non-pharmacological therapy first, with medications added for persistent moderate to severe symptoms.

blocks.text: Patients should receive structured education about the condition.
